content.comment_body: I am planning to install a home battery. The inverter chosen is a SolarEdge SE 5K-RWS StoreEdge, and a SolarEdge Modbus-Meter INLINE (RS485 Half duplex) will also be included. Creating a UTP connection is not feasible due to practical constraints. Currently, I have two [product_name] [version_no] devices set up to read my energy meters—one in the attic for solar and one on the ground floor for grid usage. My main question is: If the right modules are installed, can [product_name] function as both transmitter and receiver? If yes, which module should be used?

The [product_name] [version_no] can communicate using Ethernet TCP/IP. Versions 8.1, 8.2, and 8.3 also allow communication via Modbus TCP/IP, but do not support Modbus RTU directly. You'll require a gateway device to convert between Modbus RTU and Modbus TCP/IP.

Thank you for your clear explanation. Although this might be slightly off-topic, having two Modbus gateways could resolve my issue? Your response helped me understand more. It's never too late to learn new things. Thanks again to everyone in this forum.
[product_name] CIM module can support MODBUS RTU, though I haven't used it personally. You might want to search for more information online. [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are trying to connect [product_name] modules with a SolarEdge energy system using Modbus RTU, but face issues with communication protocols. Responses clarify that available modules natively support Ethernet and Modbus TCP/IP, but not Modbus RTU, so an additional gateway or module is required. There is some uncertainty around recommended modules, indicating potential complexity for the user.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope that [product_name] modules, possibly with an extra module, can communicate directly over Modbus RTU with minimal additional setup. They want a simple and reliable solution without needing extensive infrastructure.
